chapter: Steinway, Blue Note, awards and wrap-up
title: The Guitars project
summary: Brown asks about the 2006 album with John Scofield and Bela Fleck; Tyner cannot recall details.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Oh of course, but you are based here in the New York area. I want to talk about another project that I think is such a departure from when we look--I mean I had all my LP’s, all my CD’s out, but when the project The Guitars, because I think that one-because it’s such a departure from what you are known for and when you talk about guitar, that is going to open up a whole window for a bunch of . . . plus you bring in Bela Fleck on banjo. So how did that project come together? And it seems to have kind of been innovative in the way that you can actually go in and look and see which guitarist was playing in what session. That seems to be a major project, so if you could talk about that.
Yeah, I have forgotten the little details. I think Orrin had something to do with that, I think he was the producer on that project.
I don’t know who was the producer.
My computers dead now so I don’t know.
He is talking about something current.
That was in 2006 where you had John Scofield, Bela Fleck, Marc . . .
I think that was probably put together here.
Yeah, sometimes I forget a lot of little things . . . (laughs) details.
